context: Two migration-kit defects found by the P8.3 verifier (LOG 09:40:19Z, findings a and b; evidence/P8.3-watermark-verify.json 'delta --dry-run supported by sync.mjs'). Only scripts/migration was changed. No database other than a throwaway local PG16 (127.0.0.1:55432, trust auth, in a temp dir that was deleted afterwards) was connected to. Nothing was committed or pushed. STATE.json and LOG.md were not touched. The permission system refused nothing.

changes.what: New refuseDryRun(args, mode) helper (sync.mjs:96-104). It throws '<mode> has no dry-run; --dry-run is only supported by reverse-delta' when args.dryRun is set. It is the first statement of verify (:349), runGap (:457), runDelta (:774), runFullRefresh (:937), runInitWatermarks (:955), runInitWatermarksPostCutover (:1228) and initWatermarksForTables (:247), so it runs before any guard, DNS lookup, STATE read or connect(). main() also refuses for every mode except reverse-delta before it dispatches (:1376). The usage comment notes that --dry-run is reverse-delta only (:22). runReverseDelta and parseArgs are unchanged.
changes.why: parseArgs accepts --dry-run for every mode, but only reverse-delta reads it. 'delta --dry-run' used to run a real delta. The mutation run below shows this: 1 blog_posts row and 1 demo_requests row were inserted and 4 sync_log rows were written.

changes.what: Scenario 33 (selftest.mjs:1812) calls delta, gap, verify, full-refresh (with a copyFn that throws if it is ever called, and fake DNS), init-watermarks and init-watermarks-post-cutover with dryRun and deliberately UNSET env names. Each call must fail with the dry-run refusal and not with lib.mjs's 'Missing required env var', which proves no connect() was reached. Then, on local PG, delta --dry-run with real env names and a pending source row must leave target rows, sync_state and sync_log byte-identical. Last, the CLI 'node sync.mjs <mode> --dry-run' must exit 1 with an empty stdout and the refusal on stderr, for all 6 modes. Scenario 34 (:1917) checks that reverse-delta --dry-run still plans (rowsAboveGap 1, moved 0, dryRun true) and leaves the source untouched, with no write guards set. Existing scenario 12 (reverse-delta dry-run, guards, real write) is unchanged and still passes.
changes.why: Task: add db self-test cases for delta, gap and init --dry-run refusing before any connection, and for reverse-delta --dry-run being unchanged.

changes.what: normalizeHtmlNoise's dpl strip changed from /[?&]dpl=[^&"'\s]+/g to /[?&]dpl=[^&"'\s\\]+/g (extract.mjs:23), with a comment (:19-22). Nothing else changed.
changes.why: In RSC flight data a Vercel ref ends in an escaped quote ('...js?dpl=dpl_x\"'). The old class also consumed the backslash, which un-escaped the quote. That closed the self.__next_f.push JS string literal early, so extractEmbeddedBlogPosts threw 'found RSC flight rows but no embedded post array' and tie-permutation-real-data failed on the Vercel-served /blog. For every input where no backslash directly follows a dpl value, the output is byte-identical to before. When a backslash does follow, the new output keeps that backslash and everything after it, where the old regex removed them.

changes.what: An offline self-test with 4 cases. (1) escaped-quote-rsc-payload-with-dpl-parses: a Vercel-shaped /blog body with an I[...] import row, whose chunk refs end in '?dpl=...\"', in the same push literal as the post list. After normalizeHtmlNoise it must give exactly the raw body's posts, with no dpl= left and the escapes kept, and the inlined old regex must break it. (2) blog-tie-permutation-self-compare-on-normalized-vercel-payload: checkPageTiePermutation(kind blog-embedded-json) must pass on the new normalization and fail on the old. (3) plain-html-attribute-dpl-values-stripped-identically: 9 attribute shapes (double and single quotes, unquoted, &-joined, leading ?dpl then &, srcset, build-id path, nonce, near-miss 'adpl' / empty dpl=). Each must equal a fixed expected string and the old regex's output. (4) randomized-backslash-free-inputs-unchanged-vs-old-regex: 20000 deterministic LCG strings over a dpl/quote/whitespace alphabet with no backslash must be identical to the old output. The file ends with a SUMMARY line like the other parity self-tests.
changes.why: Task: add a self-test for an escaped-quote RSC payload with ?dpl= that now parses, and one for plain HTML attribute dpl values still being stripped identically.

reExtraction.what: Every 2xx text/html raw body in both P8.2 inputs (216 in p6 raw-a / Replit and 216 in p8 raw-b / Vercel) was run through extractHtml with the pre-fix and post-fix extract.mjs, and the full JSON outputs were compared. /blog and /blog?page=2 were also run through extractEmbeddedBlogPosts on the raw and on the normalized body.
reExtraction.result: extractHtml output was identical for all 432 bodies (extractDiffers: [] on both sides), so a fresh capture of the same bodies would give identical manifests and an identical compare. The normalized HTML string differs on all 216 Vercel bodies and on 0 Replit bodies. Every difference sits inside RSC script data, which extractHtml's fields ignore. On Vercel /blog and /blog?page=2, extractEmbeddedBlogPosts on the normalized body threw before the fix and now returns 172 posts, deep-equal to the raw-body result. On Replit it was 172 before and after.
reExtraction.differenceExplained: For raw-b of p8 and raw-b of p6 (219 of 301 and 219 of 297 files differ), every differing file is fully explained. The new output is longer than the old by exactly the number of '<dpl value>\' occurrences, and running the old semantics (the new class plus an optional trailing '\...' run) on the raw body reproduces the old output byte for byte. Unexplained: 0. p6 raw-a (Replit, no dpl) has 0 differing files.

notes: main() runs the --dry-run refusal before the mode switch, so an unknown mode given together with --dry-run reports '<mode> has no dry-run' instead of 'Unknown mode'. It refuses and exits 1 either way.

The refusal also sits inside initWatermarksForTables, as defense in depth for programmatic callers. Its only callers (runGapVerifyInit via full-refresh and init-watermarks) have already refused dryRun by that point.
The throwaway PG16 ran under /tmp, not the scratchpad, because the scratchpad's parent directory is mode 700 (root) and the postgres user cannot reach it. It was stopped and deleted afterwards.
